anatomy_examples.plain_label: Three leaflets meet at the tip of one stalk
anatomy_examples.look_for: Trace one petiole to the common point where three separate leaflets attach; compare Marsilea four-pinna leaves and Trifolium trifoliolate leaves with flowers.
anatomy_examples.photo_role: exact-species leaf top and underside showing full petiole-to-leaflet junction
anatomy_examples.caption: Trace one violet woodsorrel leaf stalk to its three leaflets; leaflet count alone is not proof of family.

anatomy_examples.plain_label: Two sets of pollen stalks and five styles
anatomy_examples.botanical_label: ten dimorphic stamens; five styles; superior ovary
anatomy_examples.look_for: Show a flower face and dissection clearly separating five longer and five shorter stamens from the five styles; do not count hidden organs.
anatomy_examples.photo_role: exact-species flower face and flower-center macro/dissection with scale
anatomy_examples.caption: Five long and five short stamens surround five styles in the woodsorrel flower.

anatomy_examples.plain_label: A dry fruit with five chambers
anatomy_examples.look_for: Show intact and opened mature capsules with scale and chamber anatomy; only teach seed ejection with an actual documented sequence. Compare Geraniaceae's beaked schizocarp.
anatomy_examples.photo_role: exact-species intact and opened mature capsule with scale; optional verified seed-release sequence
anatomy_examples.caption: A mature woodsorrel capsule has five chambers, unlike the long-beaked Geraniaceae fruit.
